title: North Korea Sending 6,000 Army Personnel to Russia, Kremlin Says
text:
statementquoted by Russian state-run news agency TASS.
Kurskis a border region that has been heavily contested by Russian and Ukrainian forces. At the end of April, Russia claimed to have retaken the area since Ukrainian forces first entered it in mid-2024.
“Chairman of the State Affairs of the DPRK Kim Jong Un has decided to send 1,000 sappers to Russia to clear mines on Russian territory, as well as 5,000 military construction workers to restore infrastructure destroyed by the occupiers,” Russian Security Council Secretary Sergey Shoigu said in the statement, TASS reported. Sappers are military combat engineers.
Shoigu had arrived in North Korea’s capital, Pyongyang, on behalf of Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss bilateral partnerships, which include the restoration of the Kursk Region, said TASS.
There are also plans to build memorials for the Korean soldiers who died in the Russia–Ukraine war in Kursk. The construction of a museum in Pyongyang, “with the participation of the Russian side was discussed,” the statement said, according to TASS.
supply of soldiersto Russia on April 28.
The deployment was part of a “comprehensive strategic partnership” Kim signed with Putin in 2024. Russia’s ongoing war with Ukraine began with the former’s incursion into Ukrainian territory in late February 2022.
Russia admitted that North Korean forces were fighting alongside its military in the Kursk region.
In April, when Russia said it retook Kursk, the Ukrainian military’s General Staff dismissed the claim and said their soldiers continue to fight within Russia’s borders.
Russia–North Korea Nexus
North Korea and Russia have never disclosed how many North Korean troops have been sent to Russia or how many of them were killed. But according to South Korean, U.S., and Ukrainian assessments, about 15,000 North Korean soldiers have been deployed to Russia. South Korea’s spy agency said in April that about 600 North Korean soldiers died on the Russia–Ukraine battlefronts.The deepening ties between North Korea and Russia have raised worries among the United States, South Korea, and their partners that Putin may, in return, provide Kim with much-needed sophisticated technologies that can help advance his nuclear and missile programs.
According to the latest statement quoted by TASS, Shoigu is visiting Pyongyang for the third time in nearly three months. There are talks of increased communication and collaboration between the two countries.
Flights and railway communication between Russia and North Korea are expected to resume.
‘Soldier for Hire’
According to South Korea’sYonhapnews agency, the latest development and continued use of North Korean workers and troops for operations against Ukraine by Russia has been termed “deeply concerning” by the U.S. State Department.
North Korea’s generating income through “soldier-for-hire schemes” to Russia and other countries constituted a violation of a U.N. Security Council (UNSC) resolution, said the State Department’s spokesperson, according to Yonhap.
The Epoch Times reached out to the State Department for further comment but did not receive a response by publication time.
According to U.N. Resolutions 1718, 1874, and 2270, member states are prohibited from receiving any arms, related materiel, arms training, or assistance from North Korea or providing it to the Communist regime.
